newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel expects no surprises from Chernomyrdin.
newsitem.headline: Waigel expects no surprises from Chernomyrdin.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday he expected no surprises from Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who has been given broad powers while President Boris Yeltsin undergoes heart surgery.
"He is a known quantity for us, a knowlegeable partner who is aware of the problems," Waigel told reporters on the sidelines of a meeting of his Christian Social Union party.
Waigel also warned against a premature discussion over a possible successor to Yeltsin as leader of Russia.
"I would consider it dangerous to fan the flames of political speculation," he said.
A senior doctor preparing Yeltsin for heart surgery on Sunday cast doubt on whether the Russian president would survive an early heart operation.
Cardiac surgeon Renat Akchurin said on Saturday that Yeltsin must have suffered a third, and unreported, heart attack just before he was elected in July to a second four-year term.
